Keywords: Feigned retreat regrouping and pursuit discipline
RagShortTexts: Feigned retreat needs formation, horses and room to turn.
Pursuit discipline and reconnaissance affect its outcome.

Variants.Content: Riders may withdraw to draw pursuit and turn again if command, formation and horses remain usable. Scouts and supporting troops can frustrate the maneuver. A confused flight may simply be defeat; judgment depends on contact and terrain.
A feigned retreat needs understood signals and reunion points. Pursuers watching only one fleeing horse can lose flank awareness and support from companions.
Commanders provide support and turning room and count horse losses. Calling every retreat a clever plan discourages reports when control is genuinely lost.
Families cannot infer safety from departing troops: pursuers and fugitives both take supplies. Gathering dependants and animals matters more than guessing a hidden plan.
